name: QUALCOMM Incorporated
blurb: QUALCOMM is the dominant designer of smartphone application processors (Snapdragon) and the world leader in mobile baseband modems — the chips that connect phones to cellular networks. The company operates a dual business model: QCT (chip sales) and QTL (technology licensing), with the latter generating high-margin royalties on every 3G/4G/5G handset sold globally. QUALCOMM is actively diversifying into automotive silicon and edge AI processors to reduce dependence on the handset market, particularly following Apple's decision to develop its own modems.
recent: Q2 FY2026 revenue reached $10.6 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $2.65. Automotive revenue hit $1.3 billion (+38% YoY), crossing $5 billion annualised for the first time. The expected partial loss of Apple modem business is weighing on forward EPS consensus, producing near-flat EPS growth estimates (-0.3%) for next fiscal year despite strong automotive and IoT momentum. Forward P/E sits at ~15.7x — undemanding for a franchise with durable licensing revenue.
